chunks.title: Our story: A school made for teenagers
chunks.text:
A school made for teenagers
Indigo Prime Academy was founded within Indigo Academy, a network of private schools in Bishkek known for strong results and caring teachers.
Families asked for a school that would take their children from the middle grades to university with an international programme, modern teaching and the values they hold dear. Indigo Prime is our answer: a school designed around the needs, interests and ambitions of teenagers.
We combine the Cambridge curriculum with the Singapore method, so that pupils not only know more but also understand more deeply, think independently and learn to work as a team.

chunks.title: Our mission
chunks.text: To educate curious, knowledgeable and responsible young people who are ready for the best universities and for life in a changing world.

chunks.title: Our vision
chunks.text: To be the leading international high school in Kyrgyzstan, where the world’s best methods meet our culture and values.

chunks.title: Our values: Five words we live by
chunks.text:
Curiosity — asking why, and searching for answers ourselves.
Excellence — high standards in every lesson and every task.
Respect — for elders, for classmates and for every person.
Responsibility — for our learning, our words and our community.
Teamwork — succeeding together and helping others grow.

chunks.title: Director’s welcome: Dear parents and pupils
chunks.text:
Dear parents and pupils
Thank you for your interest in Indigo Prime Academy. Choosing a school for the teenage years is one of the most important decisions a family makes.
Our teachers know every pupil by name. They notice when a pupil is ready for a bigger challenge and when they need a little more support. We measure success not only in exam results but in the confidence with which our pupils speak, the questions they ask and the goals they dare to set.
I warmly invite you to visit us, to see a Singapore-method lesson and to talk with our team. Our doors are always open.
Director, Indigo Prime Academy

chunks.title: Co-education: Girls and boys learning together
chunks.text:
Indigo Prime is a mixed school. Teenagers learn side by side, just as they will at university and at work, in an atmosphere of mutual respect and clear rules.
Real teamwork — Mixed teams bring different ideas to every project and discussion.
Respect and clear rules — A clear code of conduct and attentive class teachers keep the school calm and safe.
Confidence for everyone — Every pupil leads, presents and takes part, whatever the subject.
Ready for university — Pupils leave school used to working with everyone, as they will in higher education.

chunks.text: From Grade 7 to Grade 12 our pupils follow the Cambridge pathway, step by step, towards internationally recognised qualifications and university.

chunks.title: Overview: The Cambridge pathway at Indigo Prime
chunks.text:
The Cambridge pathway at Indigo Prime
Three stages build on one another. Each stage has clear learning goals, regular assessment and a final Cambridge exam.

chunks.title: School stages: From Grade 7 to graduation
chunks.text:
Cambridge Lower Secondary — Grades 7–8 — 7–8 — Cambridge Checkpoint — Strong foundations in English, mathematics and science, and the habits of independent study. — Pupils strengthen the core subjects and learn how to study: planning, note-taking, research and presenting. The stage ends with Cambridge Checkpoint tests that show each pupil’s strengths. — English, mathematics and science to Cambridge standards — Digital literacy and computing — Project and research weeks — Cambridge Checkpoint at the end of the stage
Cambridge IGCSE — Grades 9–10 — 9–10 — IGCSE exams — The world’s most popular international qualification for 14 to 16 year olds. — Pupils choose their IGCSE subjects with the help of teachers and parents. Lessons focus on deep understanding, laboratory work, essay writing and exam skills. — Core and elective IGCSE subjects — Laboratory and practical work — Career guidance and subject choice — International IGCSE examinations
Cambridge AS & A Level — Grades 11–12 — 11–12 — AS & A Level exams — Focused, university-level study in the subjects each pupil chooses. — In the final two years pupils specialise in three or four subjects at AS and A Level. A Level results are accepted by universities around the world. — Three to four specialist subjects — University counselling and applications — Preparation for IELTS / SAT and the ORT — Research projects and leadership

chunks.title: Progress: How we track progress
chunks.text:
Regular assessment — Short checks in lessons and end-of-unit tests to Cambridge standards.
Clear feedback — Pupils know what they do well and what to improve next.
Parent meetings — Reports and open conversations with families every term.
Room to excel — Olympiad groups and extra classes for pupils ready for more.

chunks.title: Cambridge & Singapore
chunks.text: Cambridge sets the international standard of what pupils learn. The Singapore method decides how they learn it: actively, together and with real understanding.

chunks.title: Cambridge curriculum: An international standard for every subject
chunks.text:
An international standard for every subject
Cambridge International Education is part of the University of Cambridge. Its programmes and exams are used by schools in more than 160 countries and accepted by universities around the world.
Every subject has a clear curriculum framework for each year. Teachers plan lessons against these goals, and pupils take externally marked exams at the end of Lower Secondary, IGCSE and A Level.
The programme values thinking skills as much as knowledge: analysing, explaining, experimenting and writing clearly.
The Cambridge learner is…
Confident in working with information and ideas
Responsible for themselves and others
Reflective, able to develop their ability to learn
Innovative and ready for new challenges
Engaged intellectually and socially

chunks.title: Singapore method: Mathematics you can see and understand
chunks.text:
Mathematics you can see and understand
Singapore is among the world leaders in international studies of mathematics. Its method moves every new idea through three steps, so that pupils truly understand before they practise.
Concrete
Hands on
Pupils first explore an idea with real objects: cubes, counters, measuring tools, paper models.
Pictorial
Draw it
Then they draw the problem. The famous bar model turns a word problem into a clear picture.
Abstract
Write it
Only then do they move to numbers and symbols, now with a solid understanding behind them.

chunks.title: In every lesson: Learning structures that involve every pupil
chunks.text:
Beyond mathematics, our teachers use Singapore collaborative learning structures in all subjects. Nobody sits quietly at the back: everyone thinks, speaks and helps.
Pair work — Pupils explain ideas to a partner, check each other and take turns answering.
Teams of four — Small mixed teams solve problems together, each pupil with a clear role.
Thinking time — A pause before answering so that every pupil, not only the fastest, has time to think.
Every voice counts — Structured turn-taking means every pupil takes part, every lesson.

chunks.title: Together: What a lesson looks like
chunks.text:
A real question — The lesson begins with a problem or question linked to life.
Explore — Pupils try ideas with objects, drawings or experiments.
Discuss — Pairs and teams compare methods and explain their thinking.
Practise — Focused practice, from simple to challenging tasks.
Reflect — Pupils check what they have learned and what comes next.

chunks.title: Admissions
chunks.text: We are glad that you are considering Indigo Prime Academy. Our admissions team will guide you through every step.

chunks.title: Step by step: How to join us
chunks.text:
Get in touch — Message us to ask about places in your child’s grade.
Visit the school — Tour the building, see a lesson and meet the admissions team.
Entrance assessment — A short assessment in English and mathematics, and a friendly interview.
Submit documents — Bring the documents from the list below to the school office.
Welcome to Indigo Prime — Sign the agreement, receive the uniform and timetable, and get ready for the first day.

chunks.title: Documents: What to prepare
chunks.text:
Copy of the birth certificate or passport
Copies of both parents’ passports
Medical record (form 026/u) and vaccination card
Personal file and report card from the previous school
3×4 cm photographs, 4 pieces
Application form completed at the school office

chunks.title: Tuition fees
chunks.text: Tuition is set for each academic year. Please contact the admissions office for current fees, discounts and payment options.

chunks.title: Which grades do you accept?
chunks.text: Indigo Prime Academy teaches Grades 7 to 12. Pupils usually join in Grade 7, but transfers to other grades are possible when places are available.

chunks.title: Is there an entrance test?
chunks.text: Yes. Pupils complete a short assessment in English and mathematics and have a friendly interview, so that we can plan the right support.

chunks.title: My child’s English is not strong yet. Can they still apply?
chunks.text: Yes. We look at each pupil’s potential. New pupils can receive extra English support to help them follow Cambridge lessons.

chunks.title: Is the school for girls and boys?
chunks.text: Yes, Indigo Prime Academy is a co-educational school. Girls and boys learn together.

chunks.title: What is the Singapore method?
chunks.text: It is a way of teaching where new ideas move from objects to pictures to symbols, and where pupils work actively in pairs and teams in every lesson.

chunks.title: Can we visit before applying?
chunks.text: Yes, and we recommend it. Message us to agree a convenient day and time to visit and see a lesson.

chunks.title: School Life
chunks.text: School is more than lessons. It is friendship, projects, competitions and the feeling of belonging to a team.

13:30 — Afternoon lessons — Sciences, languages and electives.

A real question — The lesson begins with a problem or question linked to life.
Explore — Pupils try ideas with objects, drawings or experiments.
Discuss — Pairs and teams compare methods and explain their thinking.
Practise — Focused practice, from simple to challenging tasks.
Reflect — Pupils check what they have learned and what comes next.

## Tuition fees (admissions.html)
Tuition is set for each academic year. Please contact the admissions office for current fees, discounts and payment options.

## Which grades do you accept? (admissions.html)
Indigo Prime Academy teaches Grades 7 to 12. Pupils usually join in Grade 7, but transfers to other grades are possible when places are available.

## Is there an entrance test? (admissions.html)
Yes. Pupils complete a short assessment in English and mathematics and have a friendly interview, so that we can plan the right support.

## My child’s English is not strong yet. Can they still apply? (admissions.html)
Yes. We look at each pupil’s potential. New pupils can receive extra English support to help them follow Cambridge lessons.

## Is the school for girls and boys? (admissions.html)
Yes, Indigo Prime Academy is a co-educational school. Girls and boys learn together.

## What is the Singapore method? (admissions.html)
It is a way of teaching where new ideas move from objects to pictures to symbols, and where pupils work actively in pairs and teams in every lesson.

## Can we visit before applying? (admissions.html)
Yes, and we recommend it. Message us to agree a convenient day and time to visit and see a lesson.
